record.paper_title: Current Open Questions in Complete Mixability
record.original_question: Let n be a positive integer and let M_n(μ) denote the set of distributions on ℝ that are n-completely mixable with center μ. If a distribution F on ℝ or on ℝ^d is n-completely mixable, must its center be unique? Equivalently, for distinct μ, ν ∈ ℝ, is M_n(μ) ∩ M_n(ν) empty?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 1. Is the center of mixability always unique for a distribution on R (or R^d)? In other words, for μ, ν ∈ R, μ ≠ ν, is it true that M_n(μ) ∩ M_n(ν) = ∅?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 2$ be an integer. A probability distribution $F$ on $\mathbb{R}$ (respectively on $\mathbb{R}^d$) is called $n$-completely mixable with center $\mu \in \mathbb{R}$ (respectively $\mu \in \mathbb{R}^d$) if there exist random variables $X_1, \dots, X_n$, each having distribution $F$, such that
$$X_1 + X_2 + \cdots + X_n = n\mu \quad \text{almost surely}.$$
For each $\mu$, let $M_n(\mu)$ denote the set of all distributions on $\mathbb{R}$ (respectively on $\mathbb{R}^d$) that are $n$-completely mixable with center $\mu$.

Question: Is the center of complete mixability necessarily unique? Equivalently, for any two distinct points $\mu \neq \nu$, is it true that
$$M_n(\mu) \cap M_n(\nu) = \emptyset \, ?$$
artifact.status_search_result: The problem has been resolved negatively. Puccetti, Rigo, Wang and Wang (J. Theor. Probab., 2019, "Centers of probability measures without the mean") show that for each $n\ge 2$, $n$ standard Cauchy random variables can be coupled to sum to any constant $C$ with $|C|\le n\log(n-1)/\pi$. This gives an explicit distribution (Cauchy) that is $n$-completely mixable with infinitely many distinct centers, so the center is not unique in general; however, uniqueness does hold whenever at least $n-2$ of the marginals have finite mean.

status_evidence.title: Centers of probability measures without the mean
status_evidence.snippet: For each n ≥ 2, there exist n standard Cauchy random variables adding up to a constant C if and only if |C| ≤ n log(n-1)/π.
status_evidence.claim: Provides an explicit family of distributions (standard Cauchy) that are n-completely mixable with multiple distinct centers, disproving the conjectured uniqueness in general.

status_evidence.title: Centers of probability measures without the mean (Springer)
status_evidence.snippet: If (μ1,...,μn) is jointly mixable and at least n−2 of the distributions have finite mean, then the center is unique.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes uniqueness of the mixability center under the assumption that at least n-2 marginals have finite mean.
